questions.question: Describe two weaknesses of the Weimar Constitution. (4 marks)

points.text: Article 48 allowed the President to rule by decree in an emergency, but "emergency" was never defined, so it could be abused. Proportional representation meant that no single party could win a majority, leading to unstable coalition governments that frequently collapsed.

questions.question: Explain why the Spartacist Uprising failed. (8 marks)

points.text: The Spartacist Uprising failed because: it lacked popular support - most Berlin workers did not actively join the revolt; the Spartacists failed to seize key infrastructure like communications and transport; the government called in the Freikorps who were heavily armed and ruthless; the SPD had control of the state machinery and could mobilise force against the Communists. questions.question: How far was the Weimar Republic threatened by right-wing opposition in the years 1919-1923? (12 marks)

points.text: Right-wing threats were very serious: the Kapp Putsch briefly seized Berlin in March 1920; right-wing extremists murdered Erzberger (1921) and Rathenau (1922); the Munich Putsch in 1923 showed the growing Nazi threat. questions.question: "The Weimar Constitution was doomed from the start." How far do you agree? (16 marks)

points.text: The Constitution had significant flaws: Article 48 gave the President emergency powers that Hitler exploited; PR produced fragmented parliaments and weak coalitions; the President had too much power over the Chancellor.
